title: Capacity Hedge Reserve and Satellite Pools — PRD Draft
content:
Context and motivation:

Problem statement: Dedicated customers want predictable baseline capacity while retaining inexpensive, fast burst options for spikes without permanently paying for capacity they rarely use. Current approaches (hard reserved pools + opportunistic spot) either force large financial commitments or result in noisy-neighbor pressure and brittle fallbacks. We need a product that smooths peak exposure, enforces tenant isolation guarantees, and gives operators clear levers for cost and latency trade-offs.

Proposal (high level):
Introduce two coordinated primitives — Hedge Reserve and Satellite Pools — plus a lightweight brokerage layer (Reserve Broker) that orchestrates allocations, fair-share, and graceful degradation across tenants.

Key ideas: 
- Hedge Reserve: a shared, hot standby capacity buffer purchased/managed at the cluster level that is inexpensive relative to per-tenant reserved capacity and designed for short-duration surge absorption (typical hold 30s–10m). Tenants can draw on Hedge Reserve credits (metered) when they exceed their baseline.
- Satellite Pools: small, per-tenant ephemeral pools that pre-warm model caches and KV caches for high-fidelity bursts. Satellite Pools are warm for a bounded time and can be attached/detached by Reserve Broker to minimize cold-start latency without requiring long-term reserved instances.
- Reserve Broker: policy engine that decides when to route traffic to baseline reserved capacity, to Satellite Pools, or to Hedge Reserve — and when to spill to compatible model variants (lower-fidelity quantized variants) or invoke soft-eviction.

Goals and success metrics (OKRs):
- SLO preservation: <1% increase in P99 latency for prioritized tenants during 95th-percentile surge events compared to baseline.
- Cost efficiency: reduce median customer incremental cost for handling short spikes by >= 25% vs buying extra reserved capacity.
- Isolation: no cross-tenant token leakage, and no more than 0.5% increase in error rate for co-located tenants during peak borrowing scenarios.
- Operational clarity: 95% of incidents involving burst contention should be diagnosable and actionable from Console dashboards within 10 minutes.

User stories / typical flows:
- Startup app with unpredictable daily microbursts: buys modest reserved baseline, auto-enables Hedge Reserve credits to absorb repeated short spikes. Reserve Broker draws Hedge credits and attaches a Satellite Pool for 90s to warm KV cache; latency stays low and cost is billed as burst credits.
- Enterprise customer with heavy weekday peaks but predictable baseline: configures scheduled Satellite Pool windows plus a conservative Hedge Reserve cap to flatten weekday surges without committing to full reserve expansion.
- Tenant exceeds both baseline and Hedge Reserve: Reserve Broker gracefully routes to a lower-cost compatible model variant (quantized) and sets soft-degradation headers for the app to surface to users.

Product features / spec:
1) Hedge Reserve ledger
- Pool-level credits, owner-visible ledger in Console.
- Configurable size (slots) and replenishment model (auto-buy vs manual top-up).
- Per-tenant draw limits and per-draw cooldowns to prevent a single tenant from draining the pool.
- Metering: token-equivalent units consumed per-second-of-GPU.

2) Satellite Pools
- Per-tenant ephemeral set of warm VMs/GPU contexts with pinned model weights and warmed caches.
- Lifetime: configurable TTLs (default 2 minutes) and pre-warm window options (cron or schedule).
- Low-latency attach/detach API (Console + API/SDK) for programmatic control.
- Billing: per-second while attached + small keepalive charge while idle to hold cache.

3) Reserve Broker policies (policy language sketch)
- Priority bands: baseline -> satellite -> hedge -> fallback-variant -> soft-evict.
- Signals: input rate spike, queue growth, per-tenant SLO consumption, model memory pressure, cluster headroom.
- Weighting parameters: tenant_priority_score, spike_duration, historical_burst_frequency.
- Fairness knob: proportional allotment vs first-come-first-serve.

4) Isolation & safety mechanisms
- Soft-eviction handshake: broker sends an eviction preflight to tenant route (10s window) before preempting Satellite Pool resources; tenants may preemptively degrade.
- Tenant portfolios: tenants can opt-in to portfolio-level sharing across logically related tenants (e.g., dev/staging/prod arrays) with configurable isolation boundaries.
- Security: strict KMS/HSM and memory zeroization on Satellite detach; no shared KV cache objects across tenants.

5) Observability and Ops
- Console: per-tenant Hedge draw timeline, Satellite attach history, per-draw billing breakdown, and a new Burst Contention heatmap.
- Alerts: automatic anomaly alerts when Hedge consumption exceeds X% in Y minutes; suggested mitigation runbooks.
- Tracing: include Reserve decision headers in traces to correlate latency changes with routing decisions.

6) Billing model
- Baseline reserved capacity unchanged.
- Hedge Reserve: subscription credit bundle (monthly) or on-demand pay-as-you-draw pricing with step-up discounts.
- Satellite Pools: per-second attach + short warmup price; discounts for scheduled warm windows.

Operational playbooks (initial):
- Normal spike: Reserve Broker scales Satellite Pools and draws Hedge credits; ops monitors spikes via Burst heatmap.
- Hedge depletion: automatic throttling to fallback-variant + alert to account owner; ops can manually expand Hedge if approved.
- Contention incident runbook: identify dominant drawers, apply temporary per-tenant caps, notify CS and propose invoice credit if platform malfunction.

Implementation approach / phased rollout:
Phase 0 — lab experiment (2 months): prototype Hedge metering, simple Satellite attach API, simulate topologies; internal-only.
Phase 1 — limited beta (3 months): expose to 5–10 customers, UI with ledger, basic broker rules, conservative defaults.
Phase 2 — graduated rollout (2 months): add scheduling, fairness knobs, richer observability, billing integration.
Phase 3 — GA: full policy language, portfolio sharing, runbook automation.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to price Hedge credits fairly across tenants with varying GPU model costs (token-equivalent approximation may be biased for long-seq workloads).
- Pre-warming Satellite Pools is effective but can be expensive if customers misconfigure TTLs; need safe defaults and recommended SLOs.
- Deciding default fairness mode (proportional vs priority-first) will impact churn and CS workload.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hedge becomes a source of noisy-neighboring if per-tenant limits are too permissive. Mitigation: strict per-tenant throttles and dynamic decay back-offs.
- Risk: Satellite attach/detach flapping leads to cache churn and increased GPU jitter. Mitigation: minimum attach TTLs and hysteresis in broker decisions.

Dependencies:
- Serving runtime: attach/detach APIs for warmed contexts and fast cache restore (serving-runtime team).
- Billing: ability to meter per-second GPU usage tied to tenant IDs (finance).
- Console: new visuals for ledger and heatmap (console-and-rollouts).

Next steps:
- Sync with serving-runtime and billing teams to validate metering primitives (this week).
- Prepare small internal simulation harness and run synthetic surge scenarios (2 weeks).
- Recruit 3 beta customers for Phase 1 by end of quarter.

Notes to reviewers:
This is a high-level draft intended to move our thinking away from purely per-tenant reserved expansions. Looking for feedback on: default Hedge sizes, Satellite default TTLs, proposed billing levers, and whether portfolio sharing is too complex for v1.

References and context links:
- Related designs: CONFLUENCE-1254 (autoscale decision fabric), JIRA-DEDI-442 (billing instrumentation), internal spike-sim repo.
